title: Adductors
summary: The inner-thigh muscles. They pull the thigh toward the midline, and the large adductor magnus is also a strong hip extender. Deep squats grew them more than half squats, and squats grew them more than hip thrusts.

what_it_is.overview: One region in the app, the inner thigh. It covers the adductor magnus, longus and brevis, gracilis and pectineus.

heads.name: Adductor magnus
heads.origin: The lower pubic bone and the sitting bone.
heads.insertion: The back of the thigh bone and the inner knee (adductor tubercle).
heads.fiber_direction: Large, fan-shaped; its rear part runs vertically like a hamstring.

heads.name: Adductor longus and brevis
heads.origin: The front of the pubic bone.
heads.insertion: The back of the thigh bone (linea aspera), upper to middle.
heads.fiber_direction: Run down and outward across the upper inner thigh.

heads.name: Gracilis
heads.insertion: The inner top of the shin (pes anserinus).
heads.fiber_direction: Long and thin, down the inner thigh.

heads.name: Pectineus
heads.origin: The top of the pubic bone.
heads.insertion: Just below the lesser trochanter at the top of the thigh bone.
heads.fiber_direction: Short, at the top of the inner thigh.

what_it_does.detail: The job in adduction machines and cable adduction.

what_it_does.action: Hip extension, strongest from deep hip flexion.
what_it_does.detail: Why deep squats and lunges load the adductors.

what_it_does.action: Grew more with full squats than half squats, and more with squats than hip thrusts.
what_it_does.detail: Full squats 6.2% vs 2.7% for half squats; in a set-matched comparison, squats grew the adductors more than hip thrusts.

what_it_does.action: Help flex the hip from an extended position.

synergists.name: Glutes and hamstrings
synergists.role: Extend the hip with the adductor magnus.

antagonists.name: Abductors (glute medius and minimus)
antagonists.role: Move the thigh out to the side.

stabilizer_roles.text: In squats and lunges the adductors control the knees and hips; most squats are rated 0.4 to 0.6.

relationships.indirect_note: Each working set adds the exercise's rating for this muscle to the weekly total, and ratings under 0.25 count as 0. 4 sets of back squat (0.6), 3 sets of Romanian deadlift (0.4) and 2 sets of hip adduction machine (1.0) give 2.4 + 1.2 + 2 = 5.6, which the panel shows as 5.5 (rounded to the nearest 0.5). The full list comes live from exercises.json; the rows above are examples and the ratings are coaching estimates.

how.joint_angle: Full-depth squat or deep leg press.
how.stretch_position: Bottom of the squat with the hips deeply bent.
how.stance: Shoulder width or slightly wider, toes turned out.

bias.caveat: Stance width was not tested in these studies.

how.joint_angle: Pull the thighs together from a wide position.

bias.caveat: Isolation adds adductor sets without spinal load.
A wider stance is commonly used for adductors; the size of the shift is a model.

best_exercises.why: One leg at a time with cable tension; adductors 1.0.
Deep squats grew the adductors more than half squats and more than hip thrusts.
Deep squat without spinal load; adductors 0.6.
Feet high, deep hip bend; adductors 0.6.

mistakes.text: Half squats when the adductors are a goal.
Swinging into the end of range on adduction machines.
Starting adductor isolation at a wide, heavy stretch without building up to it.

coach_cues.cue: Knees track over the toes, sit deep.
Squeeze the pads together slowly; open with control.
coach_cues.why: Controls both ends of the range.

notes: Weekly target in the app: 3 to 12 adductors sets at Advanced. Intermediate and Beginner scale the minimum by 0.8 and 0.6; the maximum stays the same. Render the numbers from targets.json, not from this text.
Kubo 2019 and Plotkin 2023 measured adductors as a group; head-level data are not separated here.
Targets are low and marked extrapolated because squats and lunges give lots of indirect work.
